races.name: Edinburgh Gin Rhubarb And Ginger Handicap

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs strong pace to be effective but may struggle with sustainable gallop here
runners_data.comment: Runner-up at Nottingham last month but soundly beaten on his three starts since
runners_data.spotlight: Finished behind Wee Mary when fifth of ten at Carlisle last week; best on good or slower ground so wouldn't be ideally suited by drying conditions.

runners_data.name: Wrestling Revenue
runners_data.note: Improved last time making running at Ripon, well-drawn to sit handy and finish strongly
runners_data.comment: Below par of late but back on last winning mark and worth a look in the betting
runners_data.spotlight: Slipped to a good mark and there was much more encouragement from him at Ripon nine days ago, making the running and beaten just over 2l at the finish; one to consider, especially if backed.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up mare in good form with useful apprentice allowance, suited by even tempo
runners_data.comment: Poor strike-rate but running well on turf of late and every chance she'll be bang there
runners_data.spotlight: Just one win to her name but she comes here in good order, most recently bumping into a well-handicapped opponent at Hamilton eight days ago (5f, good); should be in the thick of it again.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: Course specialist returning from break, two wins over track and trip but current form concerning
runners_data.comment: Two C&D wins on his CV; sharper for his recent reappearance; others are still preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Two of his three wins have come over C&D, the latest last August off a 4lb higher mark; not found his best in two runs this year but he's the type to pop up at some point.

runners_data.name: Classy Clarets
runners_data.note: Recent course second suggests readiness, hold-up style suits expected race shape perfectly
runners_data.comment: In good form in recent months, winning on AW and at Hamilton; ran creditably yesterday
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins for Iain Jardine this year, the latest at Hamilton last month off a 3lb lower mark; good second over C&D 16 days ago; more appealing than most.

runners_data.name: Fear And Fast
runners_data.note: Maiden front-runner with hood replacing visor, likely to get uncontested lead in small field
runners_data.comment: 0-17; edging down the weights but he needs to leave his reappearance well behind him
runners_data.spotlight: 18-race maiden; dropping down the weights but his two runs this year have seen him finish last at Ayr and over C&D; hood replaces a visor today; likely to pop up at some point but stable have more obvious claims with Wee Mary.

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Prominent runner lacking current form, 22 days since last outing may leave him short
runners_data.spotlight: Conditions no issue but neither run last month suggested he was the answer to today's puzzle.

runners_data.name: Hard Nut
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 213-day absence, course winner but fitness major doubt
runners_data.spotlight: His only win since July 2019 came over this C&D but it is easy enough to look elsewhere now he returns from a 213-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Fear And Fast will set the pace from the front with minimal pressure in this small field, as most runners prefer to come from behind. Sixcor may sit second early but lacks the current form to challenge strongly. The sustainable gallop will set up perfectly for the hold-up horses who dominate this lineup. This race shape strongly favours patient hold-up performers who can benefit from the even tempo and finish strongly in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Finisher Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady and hold-up horses get clear runs
scenarios.body: Wrestling Revenue or Wee Mary can use their finishing kicks to maximum effect as Fear And Fast weakens. The even gallop allows patient tactics to flourish with multiple hold-up horses fighting out the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Course Specialist Returns
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Duke rediscovers his Musselburgh form despite recent struggles
scenarios.body: His two course wins give him a significant edge if he can recapture old ability off a workable mark. The familiar track and distance combination could spark improvement after disappointing efforts elsewhere.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Fear And Fast stops quickly leaving inexperienced apprentices struggling
scenarios.body: The lack of natural pace-setters creates a scramble in the final quarter-mile. Hold-up horses with stronger jockeys like Wrestling Revenue gain advantage over those with claiming riders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Shocks
scenarios.trigger: If Fear And Fast maintains his gallop better than expected in first-time hood
scenarios.body: The hood replacement helps him concentrate and he steals crucial lengths while hold-up horses hesitate. Sixcor provides just enough company to keep him honest without applying serious pressure.

watchPoints.text: Fear And Fast breaks cleanly and gets uncontested lead - could steal race if hood aids concentration
Classy Clarets gets squeezed for room in straight as multiple hold-up horses converge simultaneously
Wrestling Revenue settles kindly for Mullen after making running last time - tactical switch crucial
Royal Duke shows early pace despite hold-up style - course knowledge might prompt different tactics
Apprentice riders on Wee Mary and Fear And Fast handle pressure in tight finish between multiple runners

races.name: Edinburgh Gin Hugo Spritz Selling Stakes

runners_data.name: Tango Hotel
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making just her second start after 52 days off, needs to build on fair debut form
runners_data.spotlight: No match for a smart filly on her Beverley debut in April (5f, good to soft) but it was still a fair run and the form has received some boosts; could be capable of a fair bit better.

runners_data.name: Furturra
runners_data.note: Best rating in field at 81, prominent style suits the pace setup, recent C&D second gives confidence
runners_data.spotlight: Finished second in a C&D maiden last month; similar form when third in a 6f seller at Chester last week; solid claims once again for a stable also represented by Turnstile.

runners_data.name: Havana Gift
runners_data.note: Prominent runner showing little improvement, needs significant step forward in selling company
runners_data.spotlight: Her Thirsk debut wasn't without encouragement but she failed to build on it at Southwell 11 days later; improvement essential.

runners_data.name: Dee's Star
runners_data.note: Drops into seller after midfield finishes in novice company, prominent style fits race shape
runners_data.comment: Sixth of 13 (5f, good) on debut; no certainty to beat Past Passion or Miss Moneypit again
runners_data.spotlight: She has shown some speed in a couple of 5f fillies' novice events to date, finishing in midfield on both occasions; drops into a seller and should have a more realistic chance today.

runners_data.name: Needin' U
runners_data.note: Fades in finish and lowest rated, likely to be outpaced despite the drop to 5f
runners_data.comment: Half-sister to a useful 6f 2yo winner but considered only if lively in the betting
runners_data.spotlight: 16-1 into 4-1 ahead of her Redcar debut 19 days ago (6f, good) but having shown some pace she dropped away in the final furlong; down to 5f/selling company so interesting to see if her supporters return.

runners_data.name: Tree Wizard
runners_data.note: Only confirmed leader with rail draw, improved with cheekpieces fitted last time
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field in a 5f maiden at Bath on debut; improved when second of seven in a Beverley claimer ten days ago (5f, good to firm; cheekpieces on for the first time); further progress will be required but it is not out of the question.

runners_data.name: Turnstile
runners_data.note: Returns to preferred 5f trip with rail berth, solid form at the distance for top stable
runners_data.comment: 0-3; did not convince with stamina for 6f when fourth at Newmarket last Friday
runners_data.spotlight: No improvement for 6f on his last two starts; shouldn't be inconvenienced by returning to 5f and he has the rail to help him; one of two leading contenders for Tim Easterby.

races.paceDynamic: Tree Wizard will set the pace from the rail with no other confirmed leaders in this small field. The prominent runners Furturra, Turnstile, Tango Hotel, Dee's Star and Havana Gift will all be tracking close behind, creating a compressed pack in the early stages. With Tree Wizard unlikely to be pressured early, he can dictate a steady tempo before the field fans out in the final two furlongs. This pace setup strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can secure good positions early, as there's no pace pressure to soften up the leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tree Wizard Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Tree Wizard gets an uncontested lead and steady fractions.
scenarios.body: The leader can kick clear at the two-furlong pole while the prominent pack scrambles behind. His recent improvement with cheekpieces and rail draw make him hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners press Tree Wizard from halfway.
scenarios.body: The sustained pressure forces Tree Wizard to crack in the final furlong as Furturra and Turnstile use their superior ratings. The fitter prominent horses benefit from the tempo lift.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Rail Bias Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If there's a significant rail bias on the round course.
scenarios.body: Tree Wizard and Turnstile both drawn low can exploit track conditions while the wider-drawn runners struggle. Track position trumps pure ability in these small-field sprints.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Tree Wizard sets pedestrian fractions and the field comes home in a bunch.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed test in the final furlong where Turnstile's 5f form and Furturra's class edge matter most. Late pace becomes crucial with multiple chances.

watchPoints.text: Tree Wizard breaks slowly from the rail and loses his tactical advantage as the only leader
Furturra and Turnstile both travel strongly into the straight as the superior-rated pair
The pace through the first two furlongs - if pedestrian it opens the door for late closers
Pierre-Louis Jamin's positioning of Tree Wizard in the early stages given his 7lb claim
Any market moves on Tango Hotel given her long absence and potential improvement

races.name: Edinburgh Gin Classic Handicap

runners_data.name: Royalty Bay
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front-runner who gets uncontested lead but hasn't won in over a year and looked underwhelming last time
runners_data.spotlight: Should be on a good mark but last year was mostly underwhelming and so too her comeback effort over C&D; opposable.

runners_data.name: Modern Times
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse drawn in stall 1 who could track prominently and avoid traffic from good draw
runners_data.comment: Stays 7f; 0-13 in handicaps and others present stronger cases despite his career-low mark
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden winner who has had lots of chances in handicaps but ran well to be sixth of 22 at York (good), running on over 7f; drawn in 1 and can race prominently; considered.

runners_data.name: Zubaru
runners_data.note: In-form hold-up horse who has won last two starts but drawn wide in stall 9 may face traffic issues
runners_data.comment: Improver who has won on turf (7f, good to firm) in his last two starts; big player again
runners_data.spotlight: Mark took a hit for back-to-back wins (7f, good to firm) but only went down by a head at Yarmouth and now just 1lb higher; hard to knock, other than being drawn wide.

runners_data.name: Abduction
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner in April whose hold-up style suits the distance but needs luck in running
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple winner who won over C&D in April and ran pretty well last time at Hamilton as 6f is too sharp these days; still on a competitive mark; chance.

runners_data.name: Society Man
runners_data.note: Inconsistent hold-up horse who has struggled recently and 49 days off the track raises fitness questions
runners_data.comment: Triple winner on slow turf; hard to be confident drop in grade will end this barren spell.
runners_data.spotlight: His best efforts in Britain have been on AW and he was ideally suited by testing ground when trained in France; none too consistent, either.

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse carrying bottom weight but has been well beaten in recent starts
runners_data.comment: Struggled since his AW win in December (7f); good mark but too much to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Won over this trip on the AW in December but has been out the back in subsequent races.

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has had wind surgery and stays the trip well
runners_data.comment: Has made the frame in four of his five starts for current yard; in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: AW winner in Ireland; mostly consistent in defeat for current yard, after wind surgery in last two races; this is his trip and unlikely to be too far away.

runners_data.name: Mae Amor
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has done best winning at 6f and may find 7f stretching stamina
runners_data.comment: Edged out Jonny Concrete at Hamilton but Iain Jardine's charge is weighted to turn tables
runners_data.spotlight: Only scraped home by a short head at Hamilton (6f) last month and was never in contention at York the following week; has done all his winning at 6f and yet to shine over 7f.

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who looked well beaten last time and hasn't won since April despite trying
runners_data.comment: Hit and miss these days; possible he'll bounce back but others have more pressing claims
runners_data.spotlight: Kept trying when third at Doncaster last time (6f) but was beaten over 3l and he's not looked well handicapped since scoring by 6l in April; he's also only 1-16 over 7f.

races.paceDynamic: Royalty Bay will take this race on from the front without pressure, setting a steady gallop that should be sustainable over 7f at Musselburgh. With 8 of the 9 runners showing hold-up tendencies, there's minimal early pace competition, allowing the leader to dictate terms and control fractions. Modern Times from stall 1 could track closely but the general lack of early speed means Royalty Bay gets an easy lead. This moderate pace scenario clearly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will develop when multiple hold-up horses converge in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Royalty Bay gets an easy lead and isn't pressured early.
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows the leader to kick clear turning for home before the hold-up brigade can organize. Front-runners and prominent racers avoid the scrimmaging behind and have first run on the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Traffic Jam
scenarios.trigger: If the large hold-up contingent gets bunched up and struggles for racing room.
scenarios.body: Eight horses coming from behind creates a bottleneck in the straight with several getting stopped in their runs. The best-drawn hold-up horses on the outside get clear runs while those on the rail struggle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits All
scenarios.trigger: If Modern Times tracks the leader prominently and creates genuine pace pressure.
scenarios.body: The race develops into a more even contest with sustainable pace throughout, allowing both front-runners and closers to show their true ability. Form horses with good recent runs can capitalize on the fair test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Dash Overcomes
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses produce simultaneous finishing kicks despite traffic issues.
scenarios.body: The sheer volume of closers creates enough momentum that one or two get through the gaps to collar the front-runner late. Strong finishers with good draws benefit most from this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Royalty Bay must be watched for early pace - if challenged early the lone leader could fold quickly
Modern Times from stall 1 could track closer than expected and turn this into a more genuine pace test
Zubaru drawn widest in stall 9 needs to be watched for how much ground the wide draw costs in the early stages
Traffic developing in the straight with 8 hold-up horses - watch for which ones get clear runs
Society Man returning after 49-day break needs monitoring for fitness first time back

races.name: Edinburgh Gin Queen Of Scots British EBF Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: La Brodeuse
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs strong pace to be effective, returning after 28 days off with proven class edge
runners_data.comment: Ex-French; unraced at 7f and on good or quicker; unexposed; market revealing on yard debut
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced French winner (1m, soft) who, after changing hands for 125,000euros, was a well-backed runner-up on her stable and seasonal debut in the Group 3 Chartwell Stakes at Lingfield (7f, good to firm) four weeks ago; leading claims if confirming that promise this afternoon.

runners_data.name: Circe
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 190-day break with proven Listed form but stamina questions at 7f
runners_data.comment: Three 6f wins this year but she'll need to take her form to new levels to win this
runners_data.spotlight: Went off the boil in Listed races at the end of last season; however, a break may have helped and she was progressive last term, with three handicap wins (6f, good/good to firm) and a good fourth of 18 in the Group 3 Sceptre Stakes at Doncaster (7f, soft); can be in the mix if she's back to her best.

runners_data.name: Havana Pusey
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who should get uncontested lead and has winning form at this distance on similar going
runners_data.comment: Fifth win when landing h'cap (7f, good) last time; bit to do but can make presence felt
runners_data.spotlight: Won a handicap at Yarmouth (7f, good) in April and another big run, despite an awkward start, when third in the Group 3 Chartwell Stakes at Lingfield last month (7f, good to firm; 1l behind runner-up Magic Basma); also effective on good to soft (yet to run well on soft); she could be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Figjam
runners_data.note: Prominent type carrying 3yo weight allowance but faces significant class rise from handicap company
runners_data.spotlight: Promising 2yo last season, finishing second in a Listed race at Doncaster (6f, heavy) in October; respectable seventh in the Group 3 Fred Darling at Newbury (7f, good) on reappearance and fourth of 15 in Listed race at Haydock (6f, good to soft) a fortnight ago, about 4l behind the runner-up Magic Basma; shaped last time as though the return to 7f could help; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Golden Palace
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer who may struggle if pace is too moderate, needs strong gallop to show finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Balance of form suggests this is a difficult assignment; upped in distance
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on for fifth of 19 in 2yo Listed race at Newmarket (6f, good) last October and she could be sharper for her reappearance run there in April (7f, good), when seventh in the Group 3 Nell Gwyn; however, others have more substance to their claims.

runners_data.name: Magic Basma
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up performer with improved Listed form this season but requires genuine pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Some solid form in defeat in Listed races and she could be thereabouts
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo who has shown improved form in Listed races this term, finishing fourth at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) and runner-up at Haydock (6f, good to soft); she's 0-11 since her debut win in August 2024 and the return to 7f poses a question, but this is an easy track and she's a major player on form.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Rose
runners_data.note: All-weather specialist making significant step up in class, likely to be outpaced by this standard
runners_data.comment: Four Southwell wins this year (6f/7f); up in weights and would be more appealing over 6f
runners_data.spotlight: Four handicap wins on the Southwell AW this January-March (7f/6f) and has also shown promise on turf (albeit 0-6 on grass); however, she needs a sizeable step forward if she's to pose a threat in this Listed contest.

runners_data.name: Beaujolais Nouveau
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in first-time cheekpieces with recent winning form, effective at this distance
runners_data.comment: Of interest on 2025 best but yet to shine this spring; headgear now reached for
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to her best when winning a handicap with something to spare in first-time cheekpieces at Ripon (6f, good) three weeks ago; also effective at 7f and she could have more to offer in the retained headgear, but she has something to find back into a Listed race.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Pusey will take the field along from the front with minimal pressure, as most of this field prefer to settle behind the pace. Circe, Figjam and Beaujolais Nouveau may track in second and third but none are natural pace pressers. This creates a tactical race where the leaders get an easy time through moderate fractions before the hold-up horses La Brodeuse, Magic Basma and Golden Palace try to sweep up late. The sustainable pace and lack of early pressure strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace without expending energy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Pusey gets soft fractions without early pressure from Circe or Figjam.
scenarios.body: The pace-setter builds an unassailable advantage as the hold-up horses find insufficient pace to close into. Front-runners and those tracking closely benefit from the tactical positioning.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Basma and La Brodeuse get the strong pace they need from aggressive tactics up front.
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses can unleash their finishing kicks as early leaders falter in the final furlong. Class and finishing speed become the decisive factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Victory
scenarios.trigger: If Circe or Figjam track the leader closely and kick at the right moment.
scenarios.body: A horse positioned in second or third can strike when Havana Pusey weakens but before the back markers arrive. Tactical speed and positioning prove optimal.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Pusey goes too fast early or multiple horses challenge the leader aggressively.
scenarios.body: The early pace becomes unsustainable and the entire field comes back to the closers dramatically. The strongest stayer from off the pace capitalizes.

watchPoints.text: Havana Pusey gets uncontested lead and builds decisive advantage before hold-up horses can respond
Magic Basma and La Brodeuse struggle to make ground if early pace proves too moderate for effective closing kick
Circe's fitness after 190-day layoff becomes apparent in final two furlongs when race pressure intensifies
Beaujolais Nouveau's cheekpieces continue to have positive effect and she can track prominent position throughout
Golden Palace's hold-up style becomes compromised if sustainable early fractions don't provide enough pace to close into

races.name: Edinburgh Cup Handicap

runners_data.name: Haayimm
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suits the likely pace scenario, with gelding operation potentially sharpening him up after 34 days off.
runners_data.comment: Beat a disappointing fav at Pontefract but this gelding is very much unexposed
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded after one run last season; floored the 1-8 favourite (who has since disappointed again) in a maiden at Pontefract and then pushed another market leader (promising gelding) close over Hamilton's extended 1m (good); finished that race out well after getting outpaced and a truer-run contest here would suit on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Evening Blues
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who could press Pandemonium but his recent Wetherby effort suggests he may not be keen to force the issue.
runners_data.comment: 1m AW maiden winner in November; off since second in a claimer in December; stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: AW winner for Ger Lyons, for whom he was 1-7; weak in the betting when fifth of 11 on yard debut at Wetherby but, although he wasn't beaten far, that was a Class 4; the hood that worked well for him in Ireland now returns.

runners_data.name: Monoceros
runners_data.note: Strong closer who showed his best form for new yard last time, with the 63-day break potentially bringing improvement.
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up on his final run for Godolphin but his first two efforts read well; joined current yard for 25,000gns and kept on takingly for third behind Strength Of Spirit over 1m here in April (handicap debut); open to improvement.

runners_data.name: Strength Of Spirit
runners_data.note: Prominent style gives him options but his recent form suggests progress has stalled after two handicap wins.
runners_data.comment: Steadily progressive until below par last time; others are preferable
runners_data.spotlight: Has done well for one who opened his account in a seller, bagging his second handicap over 1m here in April; however, progress has stalled, markedly so in his last two races (competitive ones admittedly).

runners_data.name: Magical Merlot
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needed his comeback run and should strip fitter, with Lauren Young's 5lb claim helping his cause.
runners_data.spotlight: Brighton novice winner last season at 1m; gelded in November; perhaps needed his first run back and then he stuck on gamely for a close third at Windsor (1m, good to firm); could step up again but will need to in this better race.

runners_data.name: Blues And Royals
runners_data.note: Another closer who hit traffic problems at Sandown last time, making the cleaner racing here a positive.
runners_data.comment: Progressive on AW and turf and likely he can do better again despite 5lb rise
runners_data.spotlight: Maintained his progress when repelling Victory Ace for a second AW success in May (1m) and Sandown last time didn't go entirely to plan after hitting traffic; remains of interest.

runners_data.name: Victory Ace
runners_data.note: Late-running style suits but his recent switch from Roger Varian to John Butler adds an element of uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Travelled well and got there in the nick of time on his 7f comeback; improvement left
runners_data.spotlight: Picked up from Roger Varian for 40,000gns; edged home on his handicap debut over 7f and again did his best work late at Kempton (1m) when closing in on Blues And Royals with whom he's closely matched; goes further again here with little weight to carry and he has to be feared.

runners_data.name: Pandemonium
runners_data.note: Natural leader whose shocking Group 2 and Curragh efforts raise serious questions about his current wellbeing.
runners_data.comment: Well held in the Horris Hill but gained his wins in good style and may do better still
runners_data.spotlight: Last year's two wins were over 7f on soft/good to soft before finishing tailed off in a Group 2; he worryingly suffered the same fate on handicap debut at the Craven meeting (1m, good) since when he's been gelded; has a few questions to answer now and the cheekpieces are new.

races.paceDynamic: Pandemonium is the sole confirmed front runner in this eight-horse field, which creates a sustainable pace scenario where he won't be pressured early. The prominent runners Evening Blues and Strength Of Spirit will track behind but neither is aggressive enough to force a fierce gallop. This sets up perfectly for the hold-up horses Haayimm, Monoceros, Magical Merlot, Blues And Royals and Victory Ace to get the strong finishing kick they need over this 1m1f trip. The lack of pace pressure strongly favours closers who can unleash their turn of foot in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closer's Paradise
scenarios.trigger: If Pandemonium sets an uncontested lead with Evening Blues tracking passively.
scenarios.body: The sustainable pace allows hold-up horses to wind up their finishing kicks perfectly, with Haayimm and Monoceros best positioned to exploit the tactical advantage their styles create.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Evening Blues or Strength Of Spirit press Pandemonium into a stronger gallop.
scenarios.body: The increased pace still suits closers but gives the prominent duo a chance to hold on if they can dictate terms from the front positions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wire-to-Wire Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Pandemonium gets an armchair ride and kicks clear turning for home.
scenarios.body: His two 7f wins last year show he has the class to lead throughout when getting things his own way, especially with his low TopSpeed of 42 masking potential improvement.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large pack of hold-up horses all get trapped behind the slow pace.
scenarios.body: Blues And Royals already hit traffic at Sandown last time, and bunching could favour those with cleaner passages or prominent positions.

watchPoints.text: Pandemonium's finishing position will reveal if his recent tailed-off efforts indicate serious problems or just wrong conditions.
Traffic congestion in the home straight could be crucial given six of eight runners prefer to come from behind.
Evening Blues and Strength Of Spirit's early positioning will determine whether they press Pandemonium or sit and wait.
Haayimm's jumping from the stalls will be key given his hold-up style needs a clean passage from the rear.
The large group of closers could create a cavalry charge finish where draw and racing room become decisive factors.

races.name: Edinburgh Gin Seaside Holyrood Handicap

runners_data.name: Kind Touch
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces tough task from rear in small field after 261-day absence, though proven late kick on debut win shows ability.
runners_data.spotlight: Led late when making a winning debut at Ripon last August (5f, good to firm); beaten at odds-on at Pontefract (6f, good to soft) the following month but that form looks solid; gelded afterwards; brings clear potential to this handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Major Neigh Sayer
runners_data.note: Prominent racer ideally placed to track Merlier's pace with George Scott's solid 14-day record and recent tongue-tie addition showing intent.
runners_data.comment: 7f maiden winner; weakened over 1m latest but drop to 5f still a surprise; tongue-tie on
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 7f novice as a 2yo and he was tried over 1m on his seasonal/handicap debut in April; dropped to 5f at Sandown nine days ago (tongue tied first time; well backed) and travelled well but met some trouble at a crucial stage; that race set up for the closers and this is a sharper test but he could well have more to offer as a sprinter; cheekpieces now added.

runners_data.name: Mighty Magnus
runners_data.note: Another prominent runner whose recent Thirsk third suggests readiness, with Michael Dods knowing how to place his sprinters effectively.
runners_data.comment: Beat one at Hamilton latest but this fair 5.5f juvenile winner shouldn't be written off
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in two of his three starts this year, latterly when third at Thirsk six days ago on his return to 5f; fairly exposed and more minor money perhaps his best hope.

runners_data.name: Merlier
runners_data.note: Only confirmed leader gets tactical advantage but cheekpieces first-time suggests connections want more from this seller winner.
runners_data.comment: Raced five times, mostly on AW; leading player provided form is transferred back to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't have to match his earlier efforts to win a Beverley seller 25 days ago (5f, good to firm); this will demand much more and the addition of cheekpieces is not enough to tempt.

runners_data.name: Arduis Invicta
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits race shape and course-and-distance winner drops 2lbs after creditable efforts at Chester and York.
runners_data.comment: Given her wide draw it was a positive performance at Chester recently; not ruled out e-w
runners_data.spotlight: She has performed with credit in stronger handicaps at Chester and York on her last two starts and can race off 2lb lower today; C&D winner; not discounted.

runners_data.name: Justmyluck
runners_data.note: Early-positioned runner but poor recent form since January Newcastle win makes this risky despite 10lb weight advantage.
runners_data.comment: Made all on h'cap debut at Newcastle (5f, AW) in January but two lesser runs have followed
runners_data.spotlight: Made all in a 5f handicap at Newcastle in January but little to cheer in three runs since; risky.

runners_data.name: Dandy Breeze
runners_data.note: Prominent racer needs to transfer all-weather form to turf after disappointing Hamilton debut on grass three weeks ago.
runners_data.comment: Excellent second at Newcastle 16 days ago; likely capable of better still on turf debut
runners_data.spotlight: Useful ability in three AW starts, including a 5f win, but he was 20-1 and never a threat switched to turf at Hamilton three weeks ago (6f, good); needs to bounce back quickly.

runners_data.name: Lebron Power
runners_data.note: Multiple juvenile winner returns to minimum trip after moderate longer efforts, with prominent style matching tactical requirements.
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times as a 2yo (5f and 6f, soft and good to firm); not so good in two runs this time around but this represents a drop in class and going back over 5f should be fine.

races.paceDynamic: Merlier is the only confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the break, likely securing an uncontested lead with Major Neigh Sayer, Mighty Magnus, and Arduis Invicta settling prominently behind. The pace should be sustainable rather than frantic with only one horse committed to making it, creating a rhythm that builds gradually through the furlong markers. Kind Touch represents the sole hold-up option but faces a significant task from the rear in a small field where positions matter crucially over this minimum trip. This race shape strongly favours the prominent racers who can track Merlier's tempo and pounce, as they'll have tactical positioning without pace pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Merlier Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Merlier gets an easy lead and maintains his rhythm to the furlong pole without serious challenge.
scenarios.body: The leader dictates comfortable fractions and has enough left to repel late challenges, with the prominent horses unable to generate sufficient momentum having tracked a steady pace. Merlier's front-running style maximizes his chance while Major Neigh Sayer and Lebron Power benefit from the tactical race but fall just short.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Tells
scenarios.trigger: If Major Neigh Sayer, Mighty Magnus or Arduis Invicta press Merlier from the 2f pole and sustain their challenge.
scenarios.body: The sustained pressure from prominent racers forces Merlier to quicken earlier than ideal, setting up a genuine battle where tactical speed prevails over pure front-running. The horses with prominent early positioning can capitalize on being in the right place when the serious racing begins.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Heroics
scenarios.trigger: If Kind Touch gets a strong tempo to aim at and finds racing room in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The early pace becomes genuine enough to stretch the field, allowing Kind Touch to use his proven late kick from improved position. His fresh comeback combined with the race falling apart in front gives the hold-up style its best chance to succeed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If Dandy Breeze or Justmyluck find significant improvement returning to optimal conditions.
scenarios.body: The race unfolds predictably up front but one of the lesser fancied runners produces a career-best effort, exploiting the tactical nature when others fail to fire. Form reversals at short distances can happen quickly when conditions align perfectly.

watchPoints.text: Merlier's jumping and early tempo-setting crucial as sole leader could control entire race if untroubled early.
Major Neigh Sayer's positioning behind Merlier in first furlong determines whether leader gets easy time or faces pressure.
Kind Touch's ability to secure racing room in final furlong critical for hold-up chance in compact field over minimum distance.
Lebron Power's early positioning relative to other prominent runners as traffic could be decisive in small field finish.
Track bias development through card as Musselburgh's rail position can significantly impact 5f races.

races.name: Edinburgh Gin Cannonball Handicap

runners_data.name: Nakatomi
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who should get an uncontested lead and recent Hamilton second suggests he's ready to strike
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but good second at Hamilton 15 days ago; not out of things
runners_data.spotlight: Has yet to win a race but he comes here on the back of a good second of eight in 1m handicap at Hamilton; should go well.

runners_data.name: Little Ted
runners_data.note: Classy hold-up performer but age concerns at nine, needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: 9-96; well down the field at Ripon (1m; beaten 17l) latest; far better to focus elsewhere.
runners_data.spotlight: Age might be catching up but he's a multiple winner on a potentially good mark and Tuesday's run on the AW was respectable.

runners_data.name: Samra Star
runners_data.note: Strong on AW but poor turf record is worrying, hold-up style needs genuine gallop
runners_data.comment: Three-time AW winner but she doees not have comparable form on grass
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time winner on AW but 0-8 on turf and was beaten over 7l into second here two weeks ago.

runners_data.name: On The Bubble
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with course form but poor overall record raises reliability questions
runners_data.comment: Conditions shouldn't faze her and her reappearance 2nd has been franked; one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: 2-32 and one of those wins was over hurdles; runner-up over 1m1f here in April but wilted into a remote third last time.

runners_data.name: Monhammer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 213-day break, stamina questions over this trip
runners_data.comment: Slow ground would be a worry but worthy of respect otherwise off a fair mark
runners_data.spotlight: No win since May 2024 but ran well on occasions last year, albeit over 7f which is more his trip; others might see this out better but has each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Zebra Star
runners_data.note: May need further than a mile now, three-pound claimer Waugh takes off useful weight
runners_data.comment: Won on reappearance here in 2024 and decent run after a break in 2025; could go well
runners_data.spotlight: Thoroughly exposed three-time winner who may need further now, with her last win coming at 1m2f; reappearance effort was underwhelming.

runners_data.name: War Memorial
runners_data.note: Won here over seven furlongs, cheekpieces off after Doncaster failure, stamina unproven
runners_data.comment: Off the mark when beating a clear second at Musselburgh; big player again up 4lb
runners_data.spotlight: Backed when winning over 7f here in April (good) and first-time cheekpieces perhaps backfired at Doncaster; those aids are now left off but has stamina to prove over this far.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Sprint specialist stepping up in trip, likely to get outstayed by this field
runners_data.comment: Held by Jet Warrior on latest Ayr running and only win came in a 0-50 classified event
runners_data.spotlight: Only 1-32 and vast majority of his form is at sprint distances; likely to get outstayed.

runners_data.name: Pebble Dash
runners_data.note: Maiden after fourteen starts with no turf form, hard to recommend
runners_data.comment: Below par last time but two solid AW runs in March; steps up in trip with stamina to prove
runners_data.spotlight: 0-14 and hard to enthuse over after latest 10l defeat here when behind two of these.

runners_data.name: Mavetheforcebewivu
runners_data.note: Fifteen-race maiden with modest recent efforts, visor first time won't transform him
runners_data.comment: Should be all the better for her recent return to action but others are preferred
runners_data.spotlight: 15-race maiden who hasn't threatened too often and April's efforts were modest.

runners_data.name: Freak Encounter
runners_data.note: Inconsistent prominent racer returning from 111-day layoff, wind surgery showed no benefit
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent 4yo who is 1-24 and showed no benefit for wind surgery when last seen in February.

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Basement mark suggests limited ability, very lightly raced for six-year-old
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 6yo who has yet to offer much, last of seven in Ayr handicap ten days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 6yo who has yet to offer much off his basement mark; very opposable.

races.paceDynamic: Nakatomi and On The Bubble will set the early fractions with Freak Encounter likely to track close behind in third. With only one confirmed front runner in Nakatomi, the pace should be sustainable rather than cutthroat, allowing the early leaders to dictate terms without severe pressure. The large contingent of hold-up horses including Little Ted, Samra Star, War Memorial, and Monhammer will need the pace to be strong enough to set up their finishing kicks. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those with tactical pace who can avoid getting caught behind the wall of closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Favours Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Nakatomi and On The Bubble are allowed to dictate a modest tempo through the first half-mile
scenarios.body: The early leaders will have too much left in reserve for the hold-up brigade to peg back, with the race becoming a sprint from the two-furlong pole. Horses positioned handy will have the decisive advantage over those relying on late rallies.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Sets Up Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go too fast early trying to make all
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will play into the hands of the patient hold-up horses who can unleash their finishing kicks. Little Ted and War Memorial will benefit most from a truly-run mile that stretches the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Suits Versatile
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys play cat-and-mouse and the pace becomes stop-start
scenarios.body: The race will develop into a tactical affair where horses with cruising speed and a turn of foot will prosper. This uneven tempo will disadvantage pure stayers and one-paced types while suiting those who can quicken.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches up turning for home with multiple challengers
scenarios.body: A blanket finish will ensue where the best-handicapped horses and strongest finishers will prevail regardless of early positioning. Draw and racing room will become crucial factors in determining the outcome.

watchPoints.text: Nakatomi could steal this if allowed to dictate his own fractions from the front without serious pressure
Little Ted's stamina at nine years old may be compromised, watch for any signs of weakening in the final furlong
War Memorial removing cheekpieces after they backfired at Doncaster could see improvement back to winning form
On The Bubble has wilted when tested recently and may not handle sustained pressure if the pace is honest
Monhammer returning from a 213-day break faces a stamina test stepping up to a mile for the first time
